name_story.story: Sajid can be understood through the Arabic form سَاجِد, whose central sense is sajid; one who prostrates. Sajid is Arabic سَاجِد (Sājid), the active participle of سَجَدَ, meaning 'one who prostrates'.

faq.a: Sajid is associated with the Arabic form سَاجِد, whose core sense is sajid; one who prostrates.

faq.q: What is the origin of Sajid?
faq.a: Sajid is associated with Arabic. Sajid is Arabic سَاجِد (Sājid), the active participle of سَجَدَ, meaning 'one who prostrates'.
Yes — the underlying form سَاجِد is Arabic.
Sajid can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Sajid should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root س ج د is Quranic (prostration), but Sājid is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Sajid mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Sajid is rendered ساجد and carries the sense ساجد، سجدہ کرنے والا.

faq.q: What does Sajid mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Sajid is rendered ساجد and carries the sense ساجد، سجده‌کننده.
A romanized syllable approximation is sa-jid. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Sajid?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Sajid, sajid. Script forms are ساجد, سَاجِد, साजिद.

faq.q: Is Sajid a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
